match.reason: The bank point covers only overtime and penalty rates, while the new point also requires working out pay from a salary and reading what a payslip shows, so no bank point teaches the whole idea.

draft.title: Pay and payslips
card: Pay = hours worked × hourly rate. At $25 an hour, 6 hours pays 6 × 25 = $150.
Some hours are paid at a higher rate, such as overtime or a weekend shift. A rate of time and a half means rate × 1.5. Double time means rate × 2.
A salary is a fixed yearly amount. Pay for one period = yearly salary ÷ number of pay periods. A salary of $52 000 paid fortnightly gives 52 000 ÷ 26 = $2000 each fortnight.
A payslip shows the pay period, hours and rates, gross pay (pay before anything is taken out), deductions and net pay (pay after deductions). Net pay = gross pay − deductions.
draft.remember: Pay is hours × rate, with a higher rate for penalty hours. Net pay is gross pay minus deductions.

a.q: Sam earns $20 an hour. On Sunday the rate is double time. How much does Sam earn for a 5 hour Sunday shift?
a.why: Double time means 20 × 2 = $40 an hour, so 5 hours pays 5 × 40 = $200. $100 is the answer if the double rate is forgotten.
a.clue: Work out the Sunday hourly rate first.

b.q: Priya's payslip shows gross pay of $1850 and deductions of $370 for the fortnight. What is her net pay?
b.why: Net pay = gross pay − deductions = 1850 − 370 = $1480. Adding the deductions gives $2220, which mixes up the direction: deductions are taken out of gross pay.
b.clue: Net pay is what is left after deductions come out.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out ($20 × 2 × 5 = $200 and $1850 − $370 = $1480), and the card's facts and the explanations are correct.
